answer: Make each identity a vertex that must lock a copper bond for every trust edge it claims, with the bond per edge rising with its total degree, so total collateral grows quadratically, not linearly. Payouts in nectar flow only along edges with real, settled work in both directions, and a bond is slashed if either side reuses the same work proof elsewhere. One honest agent pays for a few edges and earns steadily; a farm cloning a hundred identities must fund far more edges at rising per-edge cost, and cannot share one bond across clones, so its cost outruns its nectar before it profits.
